```markdown
# SEC filing ingestion — Roadmap

## Outcomes

Source: your partner's words, 2026-11-06. Background: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec.md, specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-adr.md.
Choices made:
- Python 3.14 (`.python-version`).
- uv workspace with four member packages: sec-edgar-client, sec-edgar-download, sec-edgar-index-ingest, sec-edgar-ingest (root `pyproject.toml`).

| # | Outcome | Track | Rank | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | The quarterly and daily index files, ingested into one filing-index table | A | 1 | Small: about 130 quarterly files since 1993 plus one daily file per business day, minutes of downloading at 3 requests/second; basis: the SEC full-index and daily-index directories |
| O2 | The individual submissions that the index rows name, downloaded | A | 2 | Large: millions of files, weeks of downloading for the full history at 3 requests/second; basis: index row count × request rate, not yet measured (Stage 3 measures it) |
| O3 | 10-K and 8-K filings picked out of the submissions, with their main documents extracted | A | 3 | Unknown until the submissions are on disk; measured by Stage 4 |

Tracks: A — SEC filing ingestion (known progression). One track: each outcome consumes the one before it.

## Stages

- [ ] Stage 1: Index core
      Objective: Ingest one real archived quarterly index and one real daily index into one filing-index table.
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: nothing (package scaffolds only)
      Produces: a filing-index table holding rows from both real sources; specs/sec-filing-ingestion-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: the table answers a query for filings by form type and date across both sources; the findings file records bytes, rows, elapsed time and request count of the real run
      Leaves out: full index history → Stage 2; historical-format fixtures → Stage 2; manifests and replay → Stage 5; resumable checkpoints → Stage 5; corrections and point-in-time awareness → Stage 6; scheduling and deployment → Stage 7
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Full index history
      Objective: Extend the index table to the full index history, from the first archived quarter through daily catch-up to the present.
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: Stage 1's filing-index table
      Produces: the full index history in the table; historical-format fixtures covering the formats in that range
      Exit: every quarterly and daily index from the chosen start through the present is in the table or listed in a report as unresolved, with no duplicate rows where quarterly and daily sources overlap
      Leaves out: manifests and replay → Stage 5; resumable checkpoints → Stage 5; corrections and point-in-time awareness → Stage 6; scheduling and deployment → Stage 7
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 3: Submissions for one quarter
      Objective: Download the submissions that one real quarter's index rows name.
      Outcomes: O2
      Consumes: Stage 2's filing-index table
      Produces: one quarter's submissions on disk, linked to their index rows; specs/sec-filing-ingestion-stage-3-findings.md
      Exit: each index row of the chosen quarter has its submission on disk or is listed as failed; the findings file records files, bytes, elapsed time and per-file request cost, projected to the full history
      Leaves out: full submission history → Stage 7; manifests and replay → Stage 5; resumable checkpoints → Stage 5; scheduling and deployment → Stage 7
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 4: 10-K and 8-K handling
      Objective: Pick 10-K and 8-K filings out of Stage 3's submissions and extract their main documents.
      Outcomes: O3
      Consumes: Stage 3's submissions on disk
      Produces: extracted main documents for that quarter's 10-K and 8-K filings; specs/sec-filing-ingestion-stage-4-findings.md
      Exit: every 10-K and 8-K in the quarter has its main document extracted or is listed with a reason; the findings file records counts, failures, elapsed time and storage
      Leaves out: full submission history → Stage 7; manifests and replay → Stage 5; scheduling and deployment → Stage 7
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 5: Manifests, replay and resumable checkpoints
      Objective: Add manifests and replay, and resumable checkpoints, across index ingestion, submission download and 10-K/8-K extraction.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O3
      Consumes: Stages 1–4 as shipped
      Produces: manifests and replay; resumable checkpoints
      Exit: O1: a parser change rebuilds the index table from retained source bytes with no SEC requests; O2: an interrupted download resumes without re-fetching completed files; O3: extraction reruns from retained submissions and yields the same output
      Leaves out: corrections and point-in-time awareness → Stage 6; scheduling and deployment → Stage 7; full submission history → Stage 7
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 6: Corrections and point-in-time awareness
      Objective: Re-read quarterly indexes, record their later changes, and let readers see the table as of any earlier date.
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: Stage 5's manifests and replay
      Produces: corrections and point-in-time awareness
      Exit: a changed quarterly index yields a recorded set of additions, updates and removals, and a query as of a date before the change returns the earlier rows
      Leaves out: scheduling and deployment → Stage 7
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 7: Scheduling, deployment and full submission history
      Objective: Deploy scheduled daily ingestion and corrections, and run the full submission history download.
      Outcomes: O1, O2
      Consumes: Stage 5's resumable checkpoints; Stage 6's corrections
      Produces: scheduling and deployment; full submission history
      Exit: O1: scheduled daily and correction runs execute unattended, with their reports on record; O2: every index row in the full history has its submission downloaded or listed as failed
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: brainstorming

## Stage-spec stamp

Every stage spec's Rollout note carries this line, which writing-plans then copies verbatim into the stage plan's header:

> Roadmap: specs/sec-filing-ingestion-roadmap.md, Stage N — on plan completion, tick the stage and re-validate later stages against what shipped.

## Completion

When every stage is ticked, re-run the gap rubric over O1–O3 (SKILL.md §6). Each outcome counts as met only with path:line or test-name evidence, and its verdict names the stage plan that built it. A stage stamp alone is not evidence. An unmet outcome exits as a new stage, which keeps the roadmap live, or as a conscious deferral with a written reason.
```
